claims.text: High-purity intrinsic silicon is a suitable material for investigating lattice heat conductivity.
Heat conduction in high-purity intrinsic silicon is dominated by phonon transport when free-carrier effects are minimal.
SRO precipitates can be introduced in a controlled manner into a silicon semiconductor matrix.
The introduced SRO precipitates are distributed within the crystal lattice.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
SRO precipitates increase the phonon collision frequency.
SRO precipitates reduce phonon scattering times.
Increased phonon scattering reduces the phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Introducing SRO precipitates into high-purity intrinsic silicon will measurably decrease its lattice thermal conductivity relative to pristine silicon.
The predicted effect applies primarily in temperature regimes where phonon conduction dominates and free-carrier contributions are negligible.
Significant electronic conduction or other strongly scattering defects may cause deviations from the predicted effect.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction depends on the size, density, and distribution of the SRO precipitates.
Interactions with other phonon-scattering mechanisms may affect the magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction.
